Name: Jungle Healing Status Cure Fix
Description:
CROSS-CHECKED 2026-09-12 - independently re-verified against the same Battle.cro 0xFFE80 hardcoded detour table that forced an OPEN CONCERN onto the companion LunarBlessingFix.json this session. Move id 816 confirmed live via cfg.GetText(TextName.MoveNames) (not assumed from this file's own earlier text). The 0xFFE80 table's 9-move literal list (754/755/830/845/849/850/878/879/907 - Bolt Beak/Fishious Rend/Stone Axe/Ceaseless Edge/Lunar Blessing/Take Heart/Collision Course/Electro Drift/Fickle Beam) does NOT include 816, so Jungle Healing does not carry the double-fire risk Lunar Blessing does; also re-confirmed 816 is absent from the older 0x101E00 alias-chain's 32-id list. Separately, this package's own Code blob was hand-disassembled and byte-diffed against live Battle.cro at SourceBase 0xC33F8: byte-identical to the live Purify routine except at the two branch-target bytes (+0x18 BNE, +0x34 BLS, both retargeted to an earlier exit at +0xA4) and the tail itself (+0xA4-0xA7, POP{r4-r11,pc} replacing Purify's own continuation into its HP-heal tail) - exactly the 'HP-heal tail and status-gated exit removed' the RESOLVED note below already claimed, now confirmed byte-for-byte instead of taken on faith. The retained loop (0xC3430-0xC3498) is a generic N-target loop keyed off Battle-State-data selectors 5 (count) and 6..6+N-1 (per-iteration battler index via 0x92298 + status read via 0x8205C); it is structurally identical to Purify's own use of the same loop for its single AnyExceptSelf target, not hardcoded to the user only. Move7 data for id 816 has Target=AllAllies, EffectSequence=309, Healing=25 - byte-for-byte identical to Life Dew (id 791, a real move already present in this ROM's move table with the same profile), which corroborates that both the HP-heal and the ally-scoping come from the move's own Target field via native engine target resolution, not from anything this patch hardcodes. Residual uncertainty, stated plainly: static analysis cannot prove the selector-5/6+i target list this loop reads is populated FROM Move.Target=AllAllies specifically versus some other list, without live/emulator testing - the strong circumstantial case is that Purify's identical loop code correctly resolves its own single target the same way, but this has not been observed running.

RESOLVED 2026-09-07 - same dispatch question as the companion LunarBlessingFix.json, settled the same way for Jungle Healing (also EffectSequence 309): a full control-flow trace of Move Dispatcher 0x87304 (called unconditionally from 3+ confirmed sites, e.g. 0x148A8/0x1496C/0x14D08, with no EffectSequence check beforehand) shows it matches purely by 16-bit move id against the master table (`ldrh r1,[sl+r4*8]` vs r5, looped and bounds-checked at 0x873D0). The move-id alias/detour chain reachable via the `b #0x101e00` at 0x87328 was fully traced through 0xFFC80 -> 0xFEC00 -> 0xFE800 and only special-cases ~32 hardcoded custom move ids in the 746-920 range; move 816 is not one of them, so it falls through to the default `cmp r1,r5` arm at 0xFE800 and lands back at 0x8732C exactly as an unmodified comparison would. EffectSequence is never read anywhere in this path, and the master-table entry layout `[id:4][handler:4]` matches pk3DS.Core/Modding/Research/MechanicInstaller.cs byte-for-byte. Conclusion: this timing-0xBF entry WILL be consulted, the same way Purify's confirmed-working entry for move 685 is. Cures user and ally status conditions at timing 0xBF while EffectSequence 309 separately provides the 25% MaxHP heal via its own self-contained battle script - two independent mechanisms, not a switch keyed by EffectSequence. Uses verified standalone status-cure routine cloned from Purify (0xC33F8) with the 50% HP-heal tail and status-gated exit removed.
